title: Sell Mineral Rights in Scio, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Scio, OH | Harrison County
metaDescription: Scio sits in Harrison County's Utica core, one of Ohio's earliest and most heavily drilled shale areas. See what that history means for your mineral rights.
heroLead: Harrison County, where Scio sits, was one of the first places operators concentrated Utica development a decade ago, so the land around Scio has more drilling history behind it than most of eastern Ohio.
intro: Scio is a small village in Harrison County, part of the deep core of the Utica/Point Pleasant play. Harrison County saw an early and intense wave of leasing and permitting starting around 2011 and 2012, alongside neighboring Carroll County, and multi-well pad development has continued here in the years since.

That longer history means many families near Scio have owned a leased or producing interest for a decade or more, and the questions we hear are often less about whether the land is prospective and more about what to do with an interest that has already run through several years of production.

sections.heading: A decade of production history near Scio
paragraphs: Wells drilled here in the early 2010s have generally moved well past their initial production peak and into a longer, shallower decline phase. If your family's interest has been producing since then, your royalty statements show a clear, established trend rather than a projection.
That established history is actually an advantage when selling, because it gives a buyer real numbers to work from instead of estimates based on nearby but different wells.

sections.heading: Original leases signed a decade or more ago
paragraphs: Leases signed during the early Harrison County boom sometimes carry royalty rates, pooling provisions, or Pugh clause language that differs from what would be negotiated today. Reviewing your original lease as part of the sale process clarifies exactly what rights transfer with the mineral interest.
We pull the recorded lease from the Harrison County Recorder's office in Cadiz as part of our title review so nothing about its terms is left to guesswork.

sections.heading: What to expect if you decide to sell
paragraphs: With an established production history, pricing a mineral or royalty interest near Scio is grounded in your actual statements, current commodity conditions, and how far along the well is in its decline, always presented as a hedged range rather than a fixed promise.
You are free to sell all or, in some cases, only part of your interest, and the process typically moves quickly once title and lease terms are confirmed.

faqs.question: My family has owned this interest near Scio since the early Harrison County leasing boom. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, in a good way. Longer production history gives us more data to work from, which usually means a more accurate and better-supported offer.

faqs.question: How do I find my original lease from years ago?
faqs.answer: We search the Harrison County Recorder's records to locate it if you do not have a copy, and review its terms as part of the sale.

faqs.question: Are wells near Scio still actively producing?
faqs.answer: Many wells from the early Harrison County development phase are still producing, though at lower rates than their initial peak, which is typical decline behavior.
